correctness.rationale: For F(z1,z2)=z1^2 P(z2/z1), normalized H^1 is int_T |P| and normalized A^1 of diagonal P(1)z² is |P(1)|/2. Complex conjugation and reversal preserve the normalization P(1)=1 and L1 norm; their convex average yields real palindromic P_u=u+(1-2u)z+uz² globally without loss for minimization. Then G(u)=average |1-4u sin²(theta/2)| is convex for all real u; its critical point has v=sin(tau), tau=cos(tau), giving min=2tau/pi and exact restricted norm pi/(4tau). Independent high-precision quadrature verified tau root, 2tau/pi integral to <1e-38 and ratio 1.06266264615663 > pi/3; five additional trial polynomials checked. These numerical checks are not the universal argument.
